text:
maria: Hey, seeing intermittent NCCL timeouts on multi-GPU jobs in eu-west-2 (p3g-8). Started after yesterday's kernel roll, only on east-west heavy allreduce patterns.
jiang: ugh. can you paste the job IDs / node ids?
maria: job 7642 & 7648. nodes node-eu-23,node-eu-24. errors look like "NCCL WARN NET/RecvData: unexpected packet len" and occasional "transport timeout".
derick: do we have packet-drop stats across the TORs?
maria: checking, attaching quick tcpdump peek but suspiciously shows bursts of retransmits not raw drops.
net-bot: kernel upgrade 2024-06-13 rolled to eu-west-2 (nodes: node-eu-20..node-eu-30).
sre-oncall: timeline matches — we pushed 6.1.58 -> 6.1.60. could be new GSO/GRO behavior on mlx5 drivers.
jiang: can you run ethtool & ip link on node-eu-23? also mtu on all RoCE interfaces pls.
maria: run results:
```
root@node-eu-23:~# ip -d link show ens786f0
4: ens786f0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 3c:fd:fe:11:22:33 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    inet 10.12.23.45/24 brd 10.12.23.255 scope global ens786f0
    ROCE: enabled
    vf 0 mac 3c:fd:fe:11:22:34
root@node-eu-23:~# ethtool -k ens786f0
Features for ens786f0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
generic-receive-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on
```
maria: mtu is 9000 across both nodes.
jiang: any tc shaping or fq_codel on bridge?
maria: none. no custom tc.
derick: can you run ibv_devinfo and ibstat?
maria: ibv_devinfo output:
```
CA 'mlx5_0'
	transport:                      InfiniBand (0)
	fw_ver:                         16.27.1020
	node_guid:                      0xabcdef1234567890
	phys_port_cnt:                  2
	link_layer:                     Ethernet
```
maria: ibstat shows ports UP.
katie: are we running GPUDirect? any recent NV peer memory stack changes?
maria: yes GPUDirect enabled; nv_peer_mem module unchanged.
sre-oncall: looking at perf counters — I see receive-side coalescing spikes and then a backlog of skb fragments around 200ms before NCCL timeouts. that smells like GRO/GSO interaction with mlx5 and recent kernel.
jiang: could be GRO merging causing big packets that the RDMA stack misinterprets for RoCE v2. can we disable GRO/GSO on the RoCE interface as experiment?
derick: do it on a canary node during off-hours. also capture `tcpdump -n -i ens786f0 -w` while toggling.
maria: disabling gso/gro now on node-eu-24:
```
sudo ethtool -K ens786f0 gso off gro off tso off
```
maria: rerunning the problematic allreduce now.
(5m)
maria: early sign: no timeouts so far for this run. latency stable.
katie: nice. can we roll this to all p3g nodes? any perf cost?
sre-oncall: small CPU overhead from disabling offloads for high-packet workloads but acceptable for short-term mitigation. need proper driver/kernel fix.
jiang: open kernel bug against mlx5 relating to GRO+RoCE v2 and reference similar reports. tag vendor and include tcpdump + ethtool output.
maria: filing ticket with logs and replay pcap. also scheduling a canary kernel rollback to confirm.
ops-bot: alert created: INFRA-9821 "RoCE GSO/GRO interaction causing NCCL timeouts" assigned to eng-infra.
derick: long term options: enforce skb fragmentation limits, tweak rx_coalesce, or upgrade mlx5 FW if vendor has fix. also consider automatic fallback to TCP-based NCCL in bursts.
jiang: for immediate rollout: create daemonset to disable gso/gro on RoCE interfaces for eu-west-2 p3g pool during maintenance window, include helm flag. also annotate autoscaler to avoid eviction during mitigation.
katie: can we put cost estimate? disabling offloads increases CPU and may reduce throughput requiring more nodes. estimate +5-10% cost for affected jobs.
maria: noted. adding to incident doc. will post post-mortem with timeline and why kernel upgrade triggered regression.
jiang: thanks. if anyone sees a different pattern (packet loss rather than coalescing), ping here.
net-bot: reminder: collect kernel oops & dmesg for any mlx5 warnings (send to INFRA-9821). :memo:
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
